assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock is a clear invention: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal removed the lattice light shift and Ye's group turned it into clocks at the 10^-18 level. It underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the prospective redefinition of the second. It fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion well and rests on demanding instrumentation, which I can judge as an experimentalist.
assessment.attribution: A two-person prize is natural: Katori for the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrations, Ye for the strontium clock performance and systematic-uncertainty control. Other groups (for example in France, the UK and Germany, and Yb and Hg labs) contributed, so the boundary needs care, and Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 for frequency combs.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent groups have confirmed performance near 10^-18, and international clock comparisons are routine. Recognition is timely; the redefinition of the second is still pending and could be argued as either a reason to wait or a reason to act.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and with ion-clock work (2012 prize) could be seen as incremental by some members.
Exact priority among lattice-clock proposals and early experiments is not something I can verify independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, with a very large and lasting impact across condensed matter. The flat-band prediction and the experimental demonstration form a coherent, original and conceptually clear discovery.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald gave the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. The supplied credit omits first author Yuan Cao and other key experimentalists, and the three-person limit forces hard choices; Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Bistritzer is the most defensible set from the names supplied.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups, and the field has grown quickly, but the full interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is unsettled and the discovery dates only to 2018. Recognition is arguably still somewhat early, though the impact is exceptional.
uncertainties: Whether Bistritzer, rather than a different theorist, belongs in the final trio.
Superconductivity mechanism and the role of strain and disorder remain debated; the supplied credit list is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard models in a clean, tunable setting, from the Mott insulator transition to Fermi-Hubbard physics and single-site imaging. It changed how many-body physics is explored and has strong lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) supplied the theoretical blueprint; Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger carried out founding experiments, with Hansch and others involved in the early Mott work. Five credited names cannot all be accommodated, so the allocation is genuinely contested. My trio combines one theorist and two experimentalists, but Greiner and Cirac have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced by many groups across two decades; earlier prizes (2001, 2018-2022) touched adjacent topics, so timing is appropriate but the field has partially been recognised.
uncertainties: Overlap with the BEC prize (2001) and with other quantum-simulation candidates (Rydberg arrays, ions).
Division of credit between lattice proposal and first experiments is not cleanly resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is an invention based on band-structure engineering in semiconductor heterostructures, with unique mid-infrared performance and wide use in spectroscopy and sensing. The device is original, clear and widely deployed.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 demonstration was a team effort at Bell Labs in which Faist, Capasso, Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson and Cho took part; the molecular beam epitaxy growth by Cho is essential. The supplied three names are a defensible but incomplete group, and Capasso also appears in the metamaterials candidate.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of development, many independent implementations and commercial use; very mature. Because it is device-oriented, some members may consider it better suited to engineering prizes.
uncertainties: Whether Sirtori, Sivco or others should be included instead of Cho.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance underpin the possibility of scalable quantum computing; the original codes and the topological-code idea are deep and conceptually original, and recent experiments are demonstrating logical-qubit improvements.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane introduced the first quantum error-correcting codes, Kitaev the topological code and anyonic fault tolerance; others (Gottesman, Calderbank, Knill, Laflamme, Preskill) are also major contributors, so the three-person limit is restrictive. Shor's name is also linked to the factoring algorithm, which the supplied item does not cover.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstration is progressing but not yet decisive for scalable computation; the theory is mature but the physical payoff is still emerging. Partly premature.
uncertainties: Theory-heavy candidate; I would want experimental confirmation to be clearer.
Credit allocation among many authors is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase established that gauge potentials and geometry have observable physical consequences; they underlie topological phases and have appeared in many experiments, including electron holography in the microscope, which I know first hand.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (Bohm deceased) for the effect; Berry for the geometric phase, with Pancharatnam, Simon and others as precursors. A two-person prize of Aharonov and Berry is workable, though the discovery is split across decades.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed many times since the early electron-interference experiments, and the concepts are mature and foundational. Recognition would be very late but still appropriate.
uncertainties: Bohm's deceased status and precursor work complicate the narrative.
Combining two discoveries in one prize may weaken the 'single discovery' framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BB84 protocol launched quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution, a clear original idea with subsequent experimental implementation and practical networks. It forms a founding piece of quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the natural pair for BB84; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is a separate contribution, and the list contains duplicate spellings of his name, which I did not use. An Ekert inclusion would need a deliberate choice.
assessment.maturity: Experimental QKD is mature and independently reproduced, and the field was partly acknowledged through the 2022 entanglement prize. Timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize and the question of Ekert's role.
Security under real devices remains a research topic, not a settled engineering one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect started a large field of topological materials, with a theoretical prediction followed by decisive experiments in HgTe and by ARPES demonstration of three-dimensional topological insulators.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the Z2 phase; Molenkamp's group observed quantum spin Hall edge transport in HgTe; Hasan's ARPES work established three-dimensional materials. Zhang, Bernevig, Fu and Hughes also made decisive contributions, and Zhang is deceased, which makes configuration difficult.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and widely used, though the 2016 topological-phase prize already recognised part of the area. Timely, with complicated credit.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and with the QAH candidates.
Whether Mele or Hasan should be chosen with Kane and Molenkamp is uncertain.
